description: Windows service availability. The one metric that matters: auto-start services that are not running. Everything else supports the triage.

panels.description: Hosts where this collector failed its last scrape. Non-zero means the numbers on this page are incomplete - see the Collector scrape health row at the bottom.
panels.title: Scrape FAIL

panels.description: The number that matters. Every one of these is a service that should be up and is not - work the hotspot table below.
panels.title: Auto-start NOT Running

panels.description: How widespread the outage is. One host = local problem, many hosts = change or dependency failure.

targets.expr: count(count by(instance) ((windows_service_state{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",state="running"} == 0) and on(instance,name) (windows_service_start_mode{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",start_mode="auto"} == 1))) or vector(0)

panels.description: Work list. Display Name and Runs As tell you who owns it; a bad Runs As account is the most common cause of a start failure.

panels.description: Per-host summary. Zero in Not Running is the healthy state.

panels.description: Current state and configured start mode for every monitored service. Filter State to stopped and Start Mode to auto to reproduce the hotspot list.

panels.description: The single line to watch. Any step up is an incident; the timestamp tells you what change caused it.

panels.description: Which hosts contributed to the fleet line. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Not Running by Host (topk 10)

panels.description: A sudden drop means several services died together - look for a shared dependency.
panels.title: Running Service Count (bottomk 10)

panels.description: Composition of monitored service states over time.
panels.title: Service States (fleet totals)

panels.description: Full inventory of monitored services, including the account and binary. Useful for audit and for spotting drift between hosts.

panels.description: PID 0 means the service is not running. Use the PID to cross-reference Collector process.
panels.title: Service Process IDs

panels.description: FAIL rows mean every metric on this dashboard is stale for that host. Fix the exporter first, then re-read the KPIs.

panels.description: Growing duration usually means the host is under load or the collector is querying more objects. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
